key_insight: Epitaxial strain tunes hydrogen’s preference for tetrahedral over octahedral sites in vanadium and suppresses the first-order hydride transition in strongly strained thin films.
engineering_relevance: Film thickness and epitaxial strain offer design levers for controlling hydrogen uptake and phase stability in metal-hydride storage and sensing devices.
method: DFT calculations of hydrogen interstitial energetics and H 1s–V 3d hybridization.
In-situ electrical measurements of epitaxial vanadium films on MgO(001).
Comparison of 10 nm and 50 nm films to probe thickness-dependent phase behavior.
evidence_signal: Calculations favor tetrahedral hydrogen sites, while electrical measurements show first-order alpha–beta transitions in 50 nm films but continuous solid-solution behavior in 10 nm films.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify strain or independently separate its effects from finite-size and interfacial contributions.
paper_title: Strain Controlled Hydrogen Interstitial Site Preference and Hydride Phase Suppression in Epitaxial Vanadium
